Here is a summary of recent announcements, news, contracts, projects, and rumors by USA government entities and prominent companies/investors in key technological sectors, along with a table of recent single-stock 2x leveraged ETFs.

### US Government and Defense Announcements

**Artificial Intelligence (AI)**
*   On June 2, 2026, President Trump signed an Executive Order titled "Promoting Advanced Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Security." This order accelerates AI-enabled cybersecurity initiatives, establishes a voluntary framework for engagement with developers of frontier AI models, and prioritizes criminal enforcement against AI-enabled cyberattacks.
*   A National Security Presidential Memorandum, signed on June 5, 2026, directs the rapid onboarding of advanced AI models, the establishment of high-security computing facilities, and the strengthening of the AI talent pipeline within the National Security Enterprise.
*   In May 2026, the Department of War announced agreements with eight leading AI companies to deploy their capabilities on the Department's classified networks.
*   The White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) and other federal agencies announced new efforts in July 2026 to support Executive Order 14363, "Launching the Genesis Mission." This national initiative aims to harness AI and advanced computing to accelerate American science and ensure U.S. leadership in defining technologies.
*   The Department of Energy (DOE) launched its component of the "Genesis Mission" and announced the selection of 278 projects in July 2026, covering areas such as nuclear energy, quantum computing, and advanced manufacturing. The largest selected project is a three-year, $60 million nuclear energy initiative involving 32 partners.

**Nuclear Energy**
*   The Department of Energy (DOE) announced a conditional loan commitment of up to $17.5 billion on June 23, 2026, to support the deployment of 10 new large-scale commercial nuclear reactors at up to five sites across the United States.
*   By July 4, 2026, the DOE successfully brought four advanced test reactors to criticality, exceeding its goal of three, as mandated by a May 2025 executive order. This included Antares Nuclear's Mark-0 on June 4, Valar Atomics' Ward 250 on June 18, and Deployable Energy's Unity reactor on June 30.
*   In July 2026, Utah, Tennessee, Oklahoma, and Louisiana were selected to host Nuclear Lifestyle Innovation Campuses, aimed at modernizing the country's nuclear fuel cycle.

**Robotics**
*   A Robotic Servicing Mission, featuring the NASA-supported Robotic Servicing of Geosynchronous Satellites (RSGS) payload, launched on July 21, 2026, aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket. Funded by DARPA and utilizing robotic arms developed by the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory, this mission aims to service and upgrade satellites in geosynchronous orbit.
*   Katalyst Space's LINK robotic servicing satellite arrived at NASA's Wallops Flight Facility on June 5, 2026, for integration onto a Northrop Grumman Pegasus XL rocket. This satellite is designed to boost the orbit of NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory.
*   NASA is expanding collaborations with commercial partners to acquire key technologies, such as spacesuits and lunar landers, for its missions.
*   NASA conducted a Robotic Tech Demo for prototype gamma-ray detectors on June 11, 2026.

**Space Tech & Satellite Communication**
*   The U.S. Space Force awarded a $287 million contract to Sphinx Defense on July 27, 2026, for the development of mission planning software for the Ground Resilient Integration Framework for Operational NC3 (GRIFFON) program, a component of the Evolved Strategic Satellite Communications (ESS) system.
*   On July 28, 2026, All Points Logistics received a $250 million firm-fixed-price contract for space vehicle processing at Vandenberg Space Force Base, California.
*   Lite Coms was awarded a $22 million contract on July 24, 2026, to provide satellite communications systems for a U.S. government customer, focusing on secure connectivity in challenging operational environments.
*   Space Systems Command awarded Boeing a $2 billion contract on June 24, 2026, for two additional satellites for the Mobile User Objective System (MUOS) constellation, extending its operations through the mid-2030s.
*   On June 9, 2026, the U.S. Space Force awarded two firm-fixed-price contracts totaling $437.7 million to Viasat Inc. and Intelsat General Communications LLC for the production of the first Protected Tactical Satellite Communications – Global (PTS-G) satellites.
*   The Space Systems Command announced modifications to existing National Security Space Launch Phase Three Lane One contracts on July 17, 2026, increasing the cumulative ceiling by $11.4 billion. Companies involved include United Launch Services LLC, Blue Origin LLC, Space Exploration Technologies Corp., Stoke Space Technologies Inc., Rocket Lab USA Inc., Impulse Space Inc., and Relativity Federal Inc.
*   NASA currently has active contract opportunities for space missions, including the Commercial LEO Destinations Request for Proposal (RFP) and the Project NEXUS solicitation, aimed at replacing the aging Tracking and Data Relay Satellite System (TDRSS) constellation.

### Magnificent 7 Companies and Prominent Investors

**Artificial Intelligence (AI)**
*   On July 12, 2026, Microsoft, Google (Alphabet), and Meta announced significant AI-focused acquisitions. Microsoft acquired an AI semiconductor startup, Google purchased an AI modeling platform for $2 billion, and Meta took a minority stake in an AI-focused infrastructure firm.
*   Microsoft is investing $2.5 billion in its new "Microsoft Frontier Company," an operating business launched on July 2, 2026, to accelerate enterprise AI adoption and expand customer-focused AI services. Microsoft also acquired Fintool, an AI copilot for equity research and analysis, in April 2026.
*   Nvidia announced partnerships with Japanese companies, including Fanuc and Yaskawa Electric, on July 16, 2026, to advance the development of robotics and AI. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang highlighted that AI will make robots "smart, easily adaptable and accessible."
*   Nvidia partnered with Chinese startup Unitree (announced July 2, 2026), combining Nvidia's Jetson Thor chip and Isaac GR00T AI platform with Unitree's H2 Plus robot to create an open humanoid robot platform.
*   Google launched Gemini 3.6 Flash and has teased Gemini 4.
*   Hyundai Motor Group and Nvidia are collaborating to develop a Robot Reference Platform that integrates their Physical AI capabilities.

**Drone Technology**
*   Amazon plans a significant ramp-up of its Prime Air drone delivery capacity in 2026. The company aims to serve communities with 30 million customers and deliver 500 million packages annually by the end of the decade, with delivery times under 30 minutes.
*   Amazon's Prime Air drone delivery system will integrate drones into its existing fulfillment network, allowing them to deploy from same-day delivery sites.

**Robotics**
*   Nvidia announced new partnerships with Japanese industrial robotics leaders Fanuc and Yaskawa Electric on July 16, 2026, to advance robotics and AI development.
*   Nvidia also partnered with Unitree (details announced July 2, 2026) to create an open humanoid robot platform, leveraging its Jetson Thor chip and Isaac GR00T AI.
*   Waymo (an Alphabet company) is expanding its autonomous vehicle operations to 25 U.S. cities by 2026 and has already expanded robotaxi services to 15 cities.
*   Hyundai Motor Group and Nvidia are collaborating on a Robot Reference Platform for Physical AI.

**Space Technology & Satellite Communication**
*   Google has been in discussions with Elon Musk's SpaceX and other launch providers regarding its "Project Suncatcher." This project aims to establish orbital data centers by networking solar-powered satellites equipped with Google's Tensor Processing Units into an orbital AI cloud. An initial prototype launch with partner Planet Labs is planned around 2027. Alphabet reportedly holds a 4.9% stake in SpaceX, valued at approximately $94 billion.
